recipes.name: Classic House Hummus
recipes.imageAlt: Classic House Hummus, professionally plated hummus-style dip.
recipes.summary: Silky, nutty, lemony, savory.
recipes.description: Silky, nutty, lemony, savory; a neutral master hummus designed to carry bold flavors.
recipes.flavorProfile: Silky, nutty, lemony, savory; a neutral master hummus designed to carry bold flavors.

ingredients.raw: 60 g hulled sesame seeds, for the tahini
16 g neutral or light olive oil, for the tahini
15 g extra-virgin olive oil, for finishing

steps.text: Make the tahini: toast about two-thirds of the hulled sesame seeds in a dry skillet over medium-low heat, stirring often, until pale gold and fragrant, 3-5 minutes; keep the rest raw. Cool 5 minutes. (If you prefer, use 75 g ready-made tahini instead and skip to the next section.)

Blend all the sesame seeds to a paste, then pour in the oil in a thin stream and blend until smooth and pourable, about 2-3 minutes, scraping down twice. This fresh tahini goes straight into the recipe below.
Drain and rinse any cooked legumes very well.
For the smoothest texture, use them warm.
Blend the base with tahini, lemon, garlic, salt, cumin and MSG until completely smooth.
With the motor running, add ice water gradually until glossy, pale and creamy.
Scrape the bowl twice and blend a full 2 minutes after the final water addition.
Rest 10 minutes, then adjust consistency only with a few grams of ice water if needed.
Serve at cool room temperature for the fullest flavor.

storage.refrigerate: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 5 days. Press plastic wrap onto the surface and add a thin film of olive oil to keep it from drying.
storage.freeze: Freeze up to 1 month. Thaw overnight in the fridge, then re-whip with 1-2 teaspoons of ice water and a little olive oil.
storage.notes: Serve at cool room temperature - straight from the fridge the flavour and texture are muted.

serveWith: Warm pita bread or toasted pita chips
A crudité board of cucumber, carrot and radish
A Mediterranean mezze spread with olives and feta
chefTips: Blend a full two minutes after the last of the ice water goes in - that extra aeration is what turns paste into a light, glossy cloud.
Warm chickpeas purée far smoother than cold ones; if you can, blend them just after cooking or reheating.
variations: Swap the lemon for lime or a splash of good vinegar to change the whole character of the bowl.
Finish with a topping bar - warm chickpeas, toasted nuts, a swirl of chilli oil, chopped herbs or dukkah.
Make it lighter by replacing 60 g of the base with steamed cauliflower or courgette.
commonMistakes: Adding the water too fast. Stream it in slowly or the hummus turns loose, grey and dull instead of pale and fluffy.
Under-blending the garlic. Blend it with the lemon juice first so the acid tames the raw bite before anything else goes in.
Skipping the rest. Straight out of the processor the flavours are sharp; ten minutes lets salt, acid and spice settle.

ingredients.raw: 55 g hulled sesame seeds, for the tahini
16 g neutral or light olive oil, for the tahini
15 g extra-virgin olive oil, for finishing

steps.text: Make the tahini: toast about two-thirds of the hulled sesame seeds in a dry skillet over medium-low heat, stirring often, until pale gold and fragrant, 3-5 minutes; keep the rest raw. Cool 5 minutes. (If you prefer, use 70 g ready-made tahini instead and skip to the next section.)

Blend all the sesame seeds to a paste, then pour in the oil in a thin stream and blend until smooth and pourable, about 2-3 minutes, scraping down twice. This fresh tahini goes straight into the recipe below.
Roast or cook the named base until fully tender; roasted vegetables should have browned edges for concentrated flavor.
Drain or steam-dry thoroughly so excess water cannot thin the dip.
Place the warm base, tahini, lemon (or the specified citrus), garlic, salt, cumin, MSG and the listed flavor additions in a high-speed blender or food processor.
Blend until no graininess remains, scraping the bowl twice.
With the motor running, add ice water in a thin stream only until the puree turns glossy and forms soft ridges that hold their shape.
Blend another 90 seconds for aeration.
Rest 10 minutes, taste for salt and acidity, then finish with the olive oil.

storage.refrigerate: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 5 days. Press plastic wrap onto the surface and add a thin film of olive oil to keep it from drying.
storage.freeze: Freeze up to 1 month. Thaw overnight in the fridge, then re-whip with 1-2 teaspoons of ice water and a little olive oil.
storage.notes: Serve at cool room temperature - straight from the fridge the flavour and texture are muted.

serveWith: Warm pita bread or toasted pita chips
A crudité board of cucumber, carrot and radish
A Mediterranean mezze spread with olives and feta
chefTips: Roast the vegetables until the edges are genuinely browned, then steam-dry them - concentrated flavour and low moisture are what make this work.
Chill the finished hummus for 30 minutes; roasted-vegetable batches taste cleaner and less sweet once cold.
Make sure the onions are cool and fairly dry before blending, or they will thin the hummus and leave it greasy.
variations: Swap the lemon for lime or a splash of good vinegar to change the whole character of the bowl.
Finish with a topping bar - warm chickpeas, toasted nuts, a swirl of chilli oil, chopped herbs or dukkah.
Make it lighter by replacing 60 g of the base with steamed cauliflower or courgette.
